recalibration8.reason: Production incident fix (PR #276), not feature growth. The SPA catch-all served index.html for any unmatched path including /assets/*.js, so after every deploy a browser holding pre-deploy content-hashed chunk names received 200 text/html for a chunk request, parsed HTML as an ES module and threw 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module' — a hard dead screen for anyone with the app already open, invisible to logs and uptime checks because a 200 looks healthy. The fix adds ~455B gzip of ENTRY-GRAPH JS: client/src/_core/staleChunkReload.ts (one regex, a sessionStorage-guarded single reload, and two window listeners) installed from main.tsx and reused by ErrorBoundary, so a stale-chunk failure self-heals instead of rendering the error screen. It must be on the entry graph — recovery has to be registered before the first lazy route import, and a lazily-loaded recovery module could itself be the stale chunk. The module was already minimised for this budget (regex alternation collapsed, messages shortened) saving ~90B; the residual is irreducible without deleting the fix. main measured 219,257B with only 209B of headroom, so any addition at all breached the ceiling. Allowance raised 512B, matching recalibrations 5-7, leaving a ~266B margin. framer-motion / vendor-motion contribution stays 0 (verified in this same run: 'vendor-motion chunks in path: 0'); any vendor-motion return or further material growth still fails this gate.
